text:
maria: quick heads-up — I opened a PR to update the SOC2/audit export docs. swap out the vague phrasing about "retention" for concrete TTL vs legal-hold examples and add a Go SDK snippet + a CLI example. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/9864 :eyes:

sam: nice, link looks good. did you also add a short example showing how the export includes the retention metadata (ttl vs legal_hold)? that was missing in prior snippets.

maria: yep — added a small table + the Go example shows the Export response containing metadata.header.retention_type, retention_value. left the Ruby/Py examples as-is so we don't duplicate too much.

danielle: quick doc nit — please use consistent error handling style across snippets. prefer explicit error return checks instead of log.Fatal in snippet examples. Also can we keep snippet length under ~10 lines? reviewers skim big blocks.

maria: ok updated to a compact Go snippet and trimmed comments. will also include a one-line curl for ops folks.

legal: @maria thanks — please avoid the phrase "we may retain". Suggest: "Redwood retains audit logs according to the customer's configured retention policy (TTL) or active legal hold; see Export and Retention section." Also add a link to the SOC2 guidance page.

maria: got it — replaced wording and added internal link to /security/soc2-retention. pushed new commit.

docs-bot: PR #9864 — link checks failed: docs/security/soc2-retention -> 404.

sam: ah that path is new; probably not yet published. can we link to the consolidated retention page instead: /docs/compliance/retention-overview ?

maria: switched link to /docs/compliance/retention-overview and force-pushed.

danielle: sample Go snippet looks good, but one more ask: show how to pass the legal-hold flag when triggering an export. ops teams expect that example.

maria: added a tiny curl and the Go call showing export opts: code below. please review quickly.

---
```go
// compact Go export example (illustrative)
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
opts := &redwood.ExportOptions{TenantID: "tenant_123", Format: "jsonl", Filters: []string{"event=login"}, RetentionMode: "ttl", RetentionValue: "90d"}
resp, err := client.Audit.Export(context.Background(), opts)
if err != nil { return err }
defer resp.Body.Close()
io.Copy(os.Stdout, resp.Body)
```

curl example (one-liner):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export?tenant_id=tenant_123&format=jsonl&filter=event%3Dlogin&retention_mode=legal_hold" \
  -o tenant_123-audit-export.jsonl
```
---

legal: that helps. please also add the short note: "Exports include a retention metadata header describing whether the export is under TTL or legal hold" so auditors can find it.

maria: added that sentence with example JSON header line.

sam: once legal signs off, who will merge? I can help if you want to coordinate the branch.

maria: I'll merge after approvals — leaving the final commit message and changelog entry in the PR. ping me if CI flaps. :thumbsup:

danielle: LGTM pending legal. small follow-up: add a 1-sentence callout in the retention FAQ about how to interpret retention_value units (d = days, m = months).

legal: approved wording. thanks everyone.

maria: merging after docs-bot green. thanks all! :sunglasses:
